memory_candidates.content: When a plan parameterizes or restructures a widely-consumed definition family (e.g. replacing limitSetBelow/limitSetAbove with a side-parameterized limitSet), count external references BEFORE choosing between renaming and specialization. In this repo the Below/Above limit-MCS names had ~57 references across seven files, five outside the task's declared file_scope. Keeping the old names as thin definitional specializations of the new parameterized family preserves the 'every consumer theorem unchanged in statement' criterion at zero cost, whereas renaming would have converted a contained refactor into a cross-subsystem sweep. The same check applies to structure-parameter reorders: Lean 4 resolves named arguments ahead of positional ones, so `FMCS (fc := fc) D` frequently still elaborates after moving `fc` behind `D`, making such a reorder near-zero line delta and ergonomic rather than structural.
